result.title: Interpretable Deepfake Detection in Videos via Explicit Forensic Features and Temporal Modeling
result.summary: Deepfake detection in videos remains challenging, as manipulated content may appear visually consistent at the frame level while exhibiting subtle temporal inconsistencies. This paper introduces an interpretable deepfake detection framework that models spatially and temporally coherent facial features in video sequences. Unlike end-to-end deep models relying on implicit representations, the proposed approach explicitly encodes physically grounded forensic cues, enabling transparent analysis and improved multi-dataset generalization. The pipeline transforms videos into identity-consistent facial trajectories, segments them into fixed-length temporal windows, and represents each frame using 68 structured descriptors spanning four complementary domains: photometric, textural, geometric, and compression-based features. These descriptors provide a compact multi-domain representation of manipulation artifacts and are processed by a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to capture temporal dependencies and subtle irregularities. Evaluation on four benchmark datasets, FaceForensics++, Celeb-DF v2, a curated subset of the DeepFake Detection Challenge (DFDC), and DeeperForensics, yields strong and consistent F1-scores of 98.0%, 91.0%, 97.6%, and 96.2%, respectively. The approach also demonstrated a good cross-dataset generalization, providing a robust and interpretable solution for video deepfake detection.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出一种可解释的视频深度伪造检测框架：将视频转为身份一致的人脸轨迹并按固定时间窗切分，每帧用涵盖光度、纹理、几何与压缩四域的 68 个显式取证描述子表示，再以 LSTM 建模时序依赖。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「显式结构化描述子 + 时序建模」替代隐式表示的做法，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与可解释的 latent 内容组织提供线索，例如如何用紧凑多域特征保留任务必要信息并做时序聚合，但该文属检测任务，与推理状态生成和答案使用无直接联系，需较多核查。
